item.title: Gemini 4 Hydrogen lands in GitHub Copilot
item.description: This edition covers the release of Gemini 4 Hydrogen in GitHub Copilot and other developer ecosystem updates.
item.content:encoded:
This edition covers the release of Gemini 4 Hydrogen in GitHub Copilot and other developer ecosystem updates.

Daily digest, written automatically from the sources; read the source before you rely on it

Gemini 4 Hydrogen lands in GitHub Copilot

Gemini 4 Hydrogen in GitHub Copilot

Google's latest Flash model, Gemini 4 Hydrogen, is now generally available in GitHub Copilot. It is designed for fast, efficient agentic coding, tool use, and multistep workflows, with improved instruction.

Source: GitHub Changelog: Gemini 4 Hydrogen in GitHub Copilot

In brief

Claude Code v2.1.325 released

The latest version fixes a security issue in how zstd-compressed responses are decoded. It also adds a spinner tip in VS Code and similar integrated terminals about re-running a notebook cell.

Source: Claude Code releases: v2.1.325

Upcoming GitHub Copilot model deprecations

GitHub announced the upcoming deprecation of selected models across all GitHub Copilot experiences, including chat, inline edits, ask and agent modes, and code completions.

Source: GitHub Changelog: Upcoming deprecation of selected GitHub Copilot models in December

GitHub Enterprise Server support in Copilot app

Users can now bring work on GitHub Enterprise Server into the GitHub Copilot app. This allows adding a GHES account to work with remote repositories, issues, and pull requests.

Source: GitHub Changelog: GitHub Enterprise Server support in the GitHub Copilot app

Transformers v5.23.0 adds Inkling2

Release v5.23.0 adds Inkling2, a small multimodal model from Thinking Machines Lab that accepts text and image inputs and generates text outputs for multiple coding languages.

Source: Transformers releases: Release v5.23.0

Read the whole issue

item.title: Skribly AI News: Codex, OpenCode, Claude Code and GitHub
item.description: This edition covers recent updates to OpenAI Codex, OpenCode, Claude Code, and new AI management features in GitHub.
item.content:encoded:
This edition covers recent updates to OpenAI Codex, OpenCode, Claude Code, and new AI management features in GitHub.

Daily digest, written automatically from the sources; read the source before you rely on it

Skribly AI News: Codex, OpenCode, Claude Code and GitHub

OpenAI Codex 0.169.0

The latest release brings an opt-in terminal workspace supporting multiple side-chat tabs. Users can switch between tabs using the keyboard or mouse and reopen saved local side chats after restarting Codex. It also adds a feature to search older tasks from the agent command center by name or prompt.

Source: OpenAI Codex releases: 0.169.0

In brief

OpenCode v2.3.0

Version v2.3.0 highlights background subagents by default, allowing subagents to return immediately and continue running in the background. Developers can keep working in the parent session while multiple subagents run concurrently. Transcripts are also quieter by default.

Source: OpenCode releases: v2.3.0

Claude Code v2.1.323

Claude Code adds Code Mode as an experimental opt-in feature where Claude writes JavaScript to call its tools. This version also introduces support for the engines parameter in plugin.json.

Source: Claude Code releases: v2.1.323

Manage AI Scan via REST API

GitHub now lets you turn GitHub code scanning’s AI Scan for repositories on or off using the REST API. This feature is available at both organization and repository levels during public preview.

Source: GitHub Changelog: Manage AI Scan for repositories using the REST API

Secret scanning detects Cloudflare tokens

Secret scanning now automatically detects Cloudflare service tokens in your repositories. The update adds a new detector for cloudflare_access_service_token secrets.

Source: GitHub Changelog: Secret scanning detects Cloudflare service tokens

item.title: Codex Updates and New Developer Tools
item.description: This issue covers the latest Codex release with incremental tool updates on Google Cloud Vertex AI, along with new repository planning features and API releases.
item.content:encoded:
This issue covers the latest Codex release with incremental tool updates on Google Cloud Vertex AI, along with new repository planning features and API releases.

Daily digest, written automatically from the sources; read the source before you rely on it

Codex Updates and New Developer Tools

Codex 0.167.2 Release

Codex now sends tool updates incrementally by default when running on Google Cloud Vertex AI. Developers can opt out of this behavior by setting incremental_tools_legacy_gcp to false under features in config.toml.

Source: OpenAI Codex releases: 0.167.2

In brief

Issue Types and Fields for Personal Accounts

Issue types and issue fields are now generally available on repositories owned by personal accounts. This update brings standardized planning capabilities to individual developers and open source maintainers.

Source: GitHub Changelog: Issue types and fields are available for personal accounts

Gemini Decisions API Released

Google introduced the Gemini Decisions API, which is powered by the Gemini Decision model. The API is designed to deliver fast and calibrated multimodal decisions.

Source: Google AI Blog: Gemini Decisions API: Fast, calibrated multimodal decisions

Tabletop Group Collaboration Experiment

Tabletop is a new Google Labs experiment focused on customizable and collaborative spaces for groups. Teams can use it to build interactive itineraries, polls, and brackets together.

Source: Google AI Blog: Try Tabletop: Customizable, collaborative spaces for groups to plan, play and do more togethe…

AlphaGenome 2 Decodes DNA

AlphaGenome 2 aims to decipher how cells read DNA in order to better understand disease. The model predicts how DNA sequences and their variations impact specific human cell types and diseases.

Source: Google DeepMind Blog: AlphaGenome 2: Deciphering how cells read DNA to better understand disease

item.title: AI agents check Signal's code with proofs, and new models
item.description: Google DeepMind used AI agents to prove security properties of the code behind Signal. Also: Claude Fable 5.2, Gemini 4 Carbon for everyone, open weights from Mistral and a coding agent from DeepSeek.
item.content:encoded:
Google DeepMind used AI agents to prove security properties of the code behind Signal. Also: Claude Fable 5.2, Gemini 4 Carbon for everyone, open weights from Mistral and a coding agent from DeepSeek.

AI agents check Signal's code with proofs

People choose what to prove, agents write the proofs

On 10 November 2026 Google DeepMind presented AlphaProof Code, a system in which people decide what to prove and AI agents do the proving. Experts first turned the security goals of the Signal protocol into formal specifications and reviewed each one; agents running on Gemini Carbon then proved them against the compiled code that runs on devices, not only against the design. The work produced over six million lines of Lean, which checks every proof by machine, and took four weeks. As a test, the team put two old, already fixed bugs back into an isolated copy of the code, and in both cases the system produced a proof that the buggy version was insecure. DeepMind is publishing the verification artifacts and a technical paper.

Source: Google DeepMind: Introducing AlphaProof Code

In brief

Claude Fable 5.2: faster, and able to lead other agents

Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2 on 9 November 2026. They are the same underlying model: Fable has stronger safeguards and is open to everyone, while Mythos goes to verified cybersecurity and life-science organisations. Anthropic reports gains in coding, reasoning and vision, and output up to 30% faster than version 5.1. Fable can also coordinate other agents; in one experiment it led over 1,000 subagents for eight days to build a prototype operating system.

Source: Anthropic: Introducing Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2

Gemini 4 Carbon opens beyond security teams

Google introduced Gemini 4 Carbon on 28 October 2026 as its strongest model, aimed at cybersecurity and long, multi-step work, and first gave it only to a group of cyber defenders. On 10 November Google made it available to developers, businesses and consumers, among other places through the Gemini API in Google AI Studio and in Android Studio. Google says internal teams have seen it run for days on engineering tasks such as finding and patching bugs in large codebases.

Sources: Google: Gemini 4 Carbon is now available · Google: Gemini 4 Carbon, our next frontier model

Mistral publishes the weights of Mistral Large 4

On 29 October 2026 Mistral released the weights of Mistral Large 4, which it calls "Le Chonk": a model with about one trillion parameters, of which about 52 billion are active per token, and a context of one million tokens. Mistral aims it at agentic coding and defensive cybersecurity. The licence is a modified MIT licence that allows commercial use; offering the model as a hosted service needs a separate licence. The weights are on Hugging Face.

Sources: Mistral AI: Le Chonk, built for coders, trusted by defenders · Hugging Face: Mistral-Large-4-1T-A52B

DeepSeek shares a coding agent that waits to be asked

DeepSeek published dsh-superagent on GitHub on 31 October 2026, under the MIT licence. It watches one GitHub repository, and when an allowed person asks for work, it opens a work item, does the work in its own session and answers in the same conversation, for example with a pull request. Its rule is to take as little human attention as possible. The README calls it a research prototype, not an official DeepSeek product.

Source: GitHub: deepseek-ai/dsh-superagent-prototype

Agent Skills gets a neutral home

On 22 October 2026 Anthropic gave the Agent Skills standard, the format in which a skill is a folder with a SKILL.md file, to the Agentic AI Foundation under the Linux Foundation. The foundation already holds the Model Context Protocol. The planned roadmap includes versioned releases, a formal proposal process and security guidance for people who write and install skills. Anyone can take part without joining the foundation.

Source: Anthropic: Donating Agent Skills to the Agentic AI Foundation

Ask GitHub from Slack and Teams

Since 6 November 2026 @GitHub in Slack and Microsoft Teams is generally available. From a conversation you can investigate a bug, create an issue, make changes and open a pull request. Issues and pull requests it creates say that they came from such a conversation and who asked.

Source: GitHub Changelog: @GitHub in Slack and Teams is generally available

EU asks how elections should deal with generative AI

On 10 November 2026 the European Commission opened a consultation on revised election guidelines under the Digital Services Act for the largest platforms and search engines. It names the fast change of technology, "particularly generative Artificial Intelligence", as one reason for the update. Views can be sent until 23 November 2026.

Source: European Commission: draft revised election guidelines under the DSA

From Skribly

The Skribly Discord server is open

The short address dc.skribly.pl takes you to the invite of the Skribly Discord server. It is the place to ask questions and talk with the people who build Skribly.

Source: dc.skribly.pl

One page for all our projects

projects.skribly.pl lists the projects our team builds and will build, each with what it is, what it is made of and where it stands. Skribly is the first; more will follow.

Source: projects.skribly.pl

Docs and the UI kit are online

docs.skribly.pl holds the guides and reference for every Skribly tool and now has search on its home page. ui.skribly.pl shows the design system live: tokens, plain CSS and React components on React Aria, in light, dark and high contrast.

Sources: docs.skribly.pl · ui.skribly.pl

Skribly Agent will be free to download

Skribly Agent, the desktop app where coding agents work side by side, will be free to download and use. There is no date yet: the installers will appear on the download page when the app is published. Skribly is a non-commercial project we build in our spare time.

Source: skribly.pl/download

One thing to try

Look inside an MCP server with MCP Inspector

MCP Inspector is the free, open-source tool of the Model Context Protocol project for checking an MCP server. Run npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector to open its web view, connect it to a server you already use and see its tools, resources and prompts. Prefer the terminal? npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector --cli node build/index.js --method tools/list lists the tools of a local server. Version 2 stores tokens and secrets in the system keychain where there is one, so read its note on secrets first.

Source: GitHub: modelcontextprotocol/inspector

item.title: AI checks planning applications, and Kimi K3.1 Pro weights
item.description: Google DeepMind and the UK government cut the time planning officers spend on routine applications by up to 58%. Also: Kimi K3.1 Pro weights, OpenAI models for biology and security, and a GitHub Actions change.
item.content:encoded:
Google DeepMind and the UK government cut the time planning officers spend on routine applications by up to 58%. Also: Kimi K3.1 Pro weights, OpenAI models for biology and security, and a GitHub Actions change.

AI in the planning office

PlanAssist does the routine checks, an officer decides

On 31 October 2026 Google DeepMind described PlanAssist, a tool built with Gemini for local planning authorities together with the UK government, Google Cloud and Faculty. For routine householder applications it checks the documents, compares them with planning policies and heritage constraints, reviews earlier objections and drafts a report with citations for the officer to edit. In pilots in Barnet, Camden and Dorset it cut the time officers spend on these assessments by up to 58%. It now moves into a 12-month beta with live applications in 15 councils, and if testing succeeds the government plans to offer it to all councils in England in 2027. A qualified planning officer reviews and approves every assessment before any decision is made.

Source: Google DeepMind: Speeding up planning decisions with AI

In brief

The weights of Kimi K3.1 Pro are on Hugging Face

Moonshot AI had promised the weights of Kimi K3.1 Pro by 4 November, and they are now on Hugging Face; the first commit of the repository is dated 2 November 2026. The model has 2.8 trillion parameters, of which 104 billion are active, a context of one million tokens, and reads text and images. The Kimi K3.1-Pro License allows use, changes and fine-tuning, but large providers that offer models as a service need a separate agreement, and very large products must show the model's name. Moonshot recommends vLLM, SGLang or TokenSpeed to run it.

Sources: Hugging Face: moonshotai/Kimi-K3.1-Pro · Hugging Face: commit history

OpenAI models for biology and for security work

On 30 October 2026 OpenAI released GPT-6 Rosalind, which brings specialised biological reasoning and scientific tool use to life sciences research. On 5 November it added GPT-6-Cyber, to investigate a vulnerability, reproduce it in an authorised test environment and verify the fix. Neither model is open to everyone: Rosalind goes to organisations approved for Rosalind Research, and GPT-6-Cyber needs Daybreak Red access and approval.

Sources: OpenAI: API changelog · OpenAI: GPT-6-Cyber

GPT-Image-2.6 edits from your sketches

On 4 November 2026 OpenAI released two image models: GPT-Image-2.6 Sunburst for detailed work and GPT-Image-2.6 Flare for fast iteration. Both can produce SVG and animated GIFs. A complexity setting goes from low to high: high helps with dense text and complex layouts, but can be slower and change more than you asked. New is editing by markup: you draw circles or sketches on a transparent layer and describe the change in words.

Sources: OpenAI: API changelog · OpenAI: Image generation guide

The Ruby SDK for MCP reaches Tier 1

On 30 October 2026 the official Ruby SDK for the Model Context Protocol reached Tier 1, the highest of MCP's three SDK tiers. From version 1.2.0 of the mcp gem it supports the 2026-07-28 specification and passes 100% of the scored conformance scenarios. Tier 1 means support for a new spec version on its release day, triage of issues within two business days and fixes for critical bugs within seven days.

Sources: MCP Blog: The Official Ruby SDK for MCP Reaches Tier 1 · GitHub: modelcontextprotocol/ruby-sdk

CWE-bench v2 asks whether agents can fix security flaws

CWE-bench v2, published by Collinear AI on the Hugging Face blog on 3 November 2026, checks whether an AI agent can find and fix a security weakness in a real open-source repository without breaking what already works. The public set has 100 tasks, each reviewed by hand, covering 91 kinds of weakness (CWEs), and scoring is automatic and reproducible. Of the 11 models tested, the best solved 67.8% of tasks at the first attempt, and even the leader fails 19% of them on every try.

Sources: Hugging Face: CWE-bench v2 · Hugging Face: collinear-ai/cwe-bench

An AI toolbox for European public administrations

On 4 November 2026 the Interoperable Europe portal of the European Commission opened an AI toolbox for public administrations. It gathers reusable open-source tools, examples from European administrations, training for officials, and guidance on the law and on buying AI solutions. It supports the Commission's Apply AI Strategy, which promised a shared repository of reusable tools.

Source: Interoperable Europe: AI toolbox to support public administrations adopting AI

From Skribly

One name for our tools: Skribly

On 4 November three of our tools took the Skribly name. With version 1.0.30 the desktop app is called Skribly Agent, and existing installs keep their settings, tokens, sessions and sign-ins. In Skribly Tracker 0.1.16 the interface and logos say Skribly, and webhooks send X-Skribly headers next to the older ones, so existing receivers keep working. In agent-skills 0.2.5 the tracker id becomes skribly; older names and credentials keep working.

Sources: docs.skribly.pl: Skribly Agent 1.0.30 · docs.skribly.pl: Skribly Tracker 0.1.16 · docs.skribly.pl: agent-skills 0.2.5

One thing to try

Find your workflows that use pull_request_target

On 2 November 2026 GitHub announced that from 2 December 2026 GitHub Actions will block the pull_request_target event by default in public repositories, unless an Actions event policy allows it. The reason: such a workflow runs with the secrets of the base repository, so untrusted code from a fork could steal them. Run grep -rn pull_request_target .github/workflows in your repository. If nothing needs the trigger, keep the default; if a workflow does, allow only that workflow in an event policy.

Source: GitHub Changelog: pull_request_target blocked by default December 2

Read the whole issue

item.title: Claude in drug labs, GPT-6.1 Terra and Genie 4
item.description: Anthropic shared early results from drug developers who used Claude to design and check drug candidates. Also: GPT-6.1 Terra, Kimi K3.1 Pro, Genie 4 and agent workflows in GitHub Actions.
item.content:encoded:
Anthropic shared early results from drug developers who used Claude to design and check drug candidates. Also: GPT-6.1 Terra, Kimi K3.1 Pro, Genie 4 and agent workflows in GitHub Actions.

Claude in the drug lab

Claude helps drug developers from design to paperwork

On 27 October 2026 Anthropic reported early results from partnerships with six drug developers and from its own drug programme. At Generate Biomedicines, scientists used Claude Code to propose a genetic component for CAR T-cell therapy that is about 70% shorter than the standard one; in lab tests the immune cells made roughly ten times as many receptors. At BigHat Biosciences, Claude proposed changes to two antibody fragments, and the best versions bound more than ten times more tightly. At Enveda, Claude checked 1,061 pages of manufacturing documentation, caught all 11 issues that human reviewers had found and seven more, and cut human review time by 89%. Anthropic stresses that the work is at an early stage and mostly preclinical, which means not yet tested in people.

Source: Anthropic: Early progress on accelerating drug development with Claude

In brief

GPT-6.1 Terra, a fast model for computer use

OpenAI released GPT-6.1 Terra on 26 October 2026 in the Responses and Chat Completions APIs. OpenAI calls it "a fast, efficient model for visual reasoning, precise computer use, and clear, natural writing". It reads text and images, has a context of about one million tokens and can use tools such as computer use and MCP. The same day it arrived in GitHub Copilot, which aims it at everyday agentic coding and work in the terminal.

Sources: OpenAI: API changelog · OpenAI: GPT-6.1 Terra · GitHub Changelog: GPT-6.1 Terra in GitHub Copilot

Kimi K3.1 Pro, with its cyber skills held back

Moonshot AI introduced Kimi K3.1 Pro in a post dated 24 October 2026 on the Kimi blog, calling it its most capable 3T-class open-weight model, with a context of one million tokens. A Highspeed variant runs two to three times faster. The model is available on Kimi.com, in Kimi Work, Kimi Code and the Kimi API, and Moonshot promised the full weights by 4 November. It also removed cyber-related data from training, because it aims not to release open weights that would push the frontier of cyber capability.

Source: Kimi: Kimi K3.1 Pro

Genie 4 builds worlds with sound

On 27 October 2026 Google DeepMind announced Genie 4, a world model that generates interactive environments in real time. New are native audio, such as music, ambient sound and character dialogue, and changing a scene in plain language, for example the weather or the camera. It is a research preview for trusted testers, and DeepMind says details and object permanence can still drift over time. Every generated video and sound carries a SynthID watermark.

Source: Google DeepMind: Genie 4, a new generation of world simulation

Agent workflows in GitHub Actions are generally available

GitHub Agentic Workflows, an open-source project from GitHub Next, became generally available on 28 October 2026. You describe an automation, such as issue triage or the analysis of a failed build, in plain language in a Markdown file, and the tool compiles it into ordinary Actions YAML. Agents run with read-only permissions by default, in a sandbox behind a firewall, and a separate threat detection job checks proposed changes before they are applied. The default engine, the Copilot CLI, needs a Copilot licence.

Source: GitHub Changelog: GitHub Agentic Workflows generally available

Replica makes prototypes from your own design system

Also on 28 October GitHub Design released Replica, an open-source tool for prototypes made with AI, under the MIT licence. Unlike generic tools, it builds prototypes from the team's existing components, patterns and documentation. You describe the idea in the GitHub Copilot app and refine the prototype next to the conversation; an optional, self-hosted Replica Hub lets teammates look and comment.

Sources: GitHub Changelog: Introducing Replica · GitHub: github/replica

Lockfiles for GitHub Actions

Workflow lockfiles for GitHub Actions became generally available on 28 October 2026. Your workflows keep readable tags, while .github/workflows/actions.lock, made with the gh actions-lock extension, records the exact commits of each action and its dependencies, and those commits run even if a tag moves. GitHub notes that a lockfile protects against unexpected changes but does not tell you whether a dependency is safe.

Sources: GitHub Changelog: GitHub Actions workflow lockfiles are generally available · GitHub: github/gh-actions-lock

From Skribly

Skribly Tracker becomes the default in Skribly Agent

Skribly Agent 1.0.27, dated 29 October in our public changelog, makes Skribly Tracker the default tracker. The changelog on docs.skribly.pl lists what changes in Skribly Agent, Skribly Tracker and agent-skills, in plain words and newest first.

Source: docs.skribly.pl: changelog

One thing to try

Run LFM3 on your own computer

LFM3-1.7B from Liquid AI, released on 27 October 2026, is a small open-weight model with 1.73 billion parameters and a context of 256K tokens, and Polish is one of its 16 languages. With Docker Model Runner one command starts it: docker model run hf.co/LiquidAI/LFM3-1.7B. For llama.cpp, Ollama or LM Studio there is a GGUF build, and for Apple Silicon an MLX build. It comes under the LFM Open License v1.0, so read the licence before you put it in a product.

Sources: Liquid AI: Introducing LFM3 · Hugging Face: LiquidAI/LFM3-1.7B

Read the whole issue

item.title: Claude Duet works on its own, and asks before it acts
item.description: Anthropic previewed Claude Duet, an agent app that keeps working while you are away. Also: a package firewall for coding agents on GitHub, new DeepSeek weights, Voxtral 3 with Polish, continuous scans in Claude Security and a map of the world's forests.
item.content:encoded:
Anthropic previewed Claude Duet, an agent app that keeps working while you are away. Also: a package firewall for coding agents on GitHub, new DeepSeek weights, Voxtral 3 with Polish, continuous scans in Claude Security and a map of the world's forests.

Claude Duet works on its own, and asks before it acts

An agent that brings you what needs attention

On 21 October 2026 Anthropic opened a research preview of Claude Duet, a new app in which Claude works as a proactive agent. It points out what needs your attention, does the tasks you give it and keeps working while you are away. Duet is built around Claude Opus 5.5 and runs as its own app on iOS and Android and on claude.ai, separate from the main Claude app. It reads and drafts on its own, but before it sends a message, makes a payment, signs a document or deletes anything, it shows exactly what it is about to do and waits for your approval; some actions, such as moving money between accounts, stay blocked even then. Access starts with a waitlist for subscribers in the US.

Source: Claude: Introducing Claude Duet

In brief

A package firewall for coding agents and CI

On 20 October 2026 GitHub put a package firewall in public preview. It sits between your machines or internal registries and the public package registries and checks every package request against a policy: a waiting period for new versions, the GitHub Advisory Database for malware and vulnerabilities, and supply-chain checks. GitHub aims it at coding agents and CI runners, which install dependencies without a person looking at each one. For now it supports npm and is for GitHub Enterprise Cloud.

Source: GitHub Changelog: GitHub package firewall in public preview

DeepSeek updates V4.1 Flash

DeepSeek published DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 on Hugging Face on 17 October 2026. The model card calls it a minor update with large gains in reasoning, coding, agentic tasks and visual benchmarks, and says it finishes tasks faster with less generated text. The recommended context is one million tokens. Both the code and the weights are under the MIT licence.

Source: Hugging Face: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017

Voxtral 3 listens and speaks, Polish included

Mistral released Voxtral 3 on 20 October 2026: speech-to-text in batch and in real time, with who-spoke-when, a text-to-speech model with voice cloning, and an SDK for voice agents. Transcription covers 50 languages and speech more than 35, and Polish is on both lists. It is available through Mistral's API and the Studio playgrounds, or deployed on your own servers.

Source: Mistral AI: Voxtral 3

Claude Security now watches code all the time

On 21 October 2026 Anthropic said Claude Security, its vulnerability scanner in public beta for Claude Enterprise, now scans repositories continuously instead of waiting for a manual scan. It marks a finding as fixed when the fix lands and reopens it if the problem comes back, builds an editable threat model of the project and explains how an attacker could reach the vulnerable code. It also gains an API, webhooks and an MCP connector for Claude.ai and Claude Code.

Source: Claude: Claude Security now scans continuously and tracks fixes

A map of the world's forest types

On 22 October 2026 Google DeepMind and Google Research, with the World Resources Institute and IIASA, published ForTy, a map that sorts every 10 by 10 metre patch of land into six forest and land-use types. It was trained on about 1.7 million labelled locations and named the right forest type 90% of the time in checks at more than 9,000 sites. An early time series for 2017 to 2025 shows where natural forest turned into plantations or farms. The data is free on Google Earth Engine under an open licence.

Source: Google DeepMind: Beyond tree cover, mapping the world's forest types

Anthropic invites life scientists as guest investigators

On 22 October 2026 Anthropic opened a call for guest investigators in the life sciences: research groups at universities, nonprofits and government labs work for 8 to 12 weeks with Anthropic researchers on a project they choose. Anthropic runs its models at no cost to them, the results are published and the data and code are released as open source. Applications were open for about 14 days.

Source: Anthropic: Open call for guest investigators in the life sciences

From Skribly

Follow Skribly on Discord

The short address dc.skribly.pl takes you to the invite of the Skribly Discord server. It is the place to ask questions and follow what the people who build Skribly are working on.

Source: dc.skribly.pl

One thing to try

Sign in to GitHub CLI with tokens that expire

Since 21 October 2026 GitHub CLI can keep you signed in with a short-lived access token that renews itself, so a leaked token stops working within hours. Update gh to version 2.103.0 or later and run gh auth login --expiring, or turn it on for every sign-in with gh config set expiring_credentials enabled. gh auth status shows when the current token expires. Scripts should ask gh auth token for a token each time instead of saving one.

Source: GitHub Changelog: GitHub CLI opt in to expiring, auto-refreshing OAuth tokens

Read the whole issue

item.title: Gemini 4 Argon arrives, and Meta opens the weights of Muse Spark
item.description: Google released Gemini 4 Argon to developers and the Gemini app. Also: open weights from Meta and Mistral, Anthropic's defences against distillation, outside evaluators inside Anthropic and Claude Code Review for teams.
item.content:encoded:
Google released Gemini 4 Argon to developers and the Gemini app. Also: open weights from Meta and Mistral, Anthropic's defences against distillation, outside evaluators inside Anthropic and Claude Code Review for teams.

Gemini 4 Argon arrives

Google's new frontier model for developers, scientists and the Gemini app

On 13 October 2026 Google released Gemini 4 Argon, which it calls its latest frontier model. Developers and businesses can use it worldwide through the Gemini API in Google AI Studio; it is also in Google Antigravity, the Gemini app and AI Mode in Search for Google AI subscribers. Through the API it takes a combined limit of one million tokens for input and output. Google reports that in its own use agentic code submissions in Antigravity rose by more than 35% and rollbacks fell by nearly a third, and that prompt-injection attacks on the Gray Swan benchmark succeeded in only 0.7% of cases. A separate post shows Argon reasoning about the physical world, with 87% on the ERQA benchmark, and steering a Spot robot.

Sources: Google: Gemini 4 Argon, built to solve your hardest problems · Google for Developers: Gemini 4 Argon for Robotics

In brief

Meta publishes the weights of Muse Spark Open

On 15 October 2026 Meta released Muse Spark Open, the open-weight version of its Muse Spark family. It is a natively multimodal model with 816 billion parameters, of which 42 billion are active, and a context of one million tokens. Meta added extra safety training before release and highlights coding and long agentic tasks. The weights come under the Muse Model License with limited commercial terms and are on Hugging Face, among other places.

Source: Meta AI: Muse Spark Open

Mistral's first models for forecasting time series

Mistral introduced Timestral on 15 October 2026, its first family of foundation models for time series. They forecast many related series at once and give a range of likely values instead of one number, also on data they have never seen. There are four sizes, from 5 to 209 million parameters, and they need no GPU to run. The licence is a modified MIT licence, and the models are on Hugging Face and GitHub.

Source: Mistral AI: Introducing Timestral

Anthropic makes copying Claude much harder

On 12 October 2026 Anthropic described how it fights distillation, the covert, large-scale harvesting of a model's answers to train another model. Its defences include a classifier with false positives under 0.1%, stricter limits for repeat offenders and tens of thousands of banned accounts. Anthropic estimates that the data distillers collect fell by about 90 to 99%, but expects a game of cat and mouse.

Source: Anthropic: Strengthening our defenses against distillation attacks

Outside evaluators get an insider's view of Anthropic

On 15 October 2026 Anthropic said it has given a team from METR, a nonprofit that evaluates AI models, "employee-like access": six people with company hardware, office space and internal tools. METR will publish its risk assessments, and Anthropic cannot veto publication, only ask to redact defined categories such as confidential material. SecureBio is reviewing the chemical and biological chapter of a risk report, and Anthropic is building three tiers of access for evaluators.

Source: Anthropic: An update on independent evaluators

Claude Code Review leaves research preview

Since 15 October 2026 Code Review in Claude Code is out of research preview for Team and Enterprise organisations. Once an admin enables it and installs the GitHub App, it reviews new pull requests automatically before a person does. Admins choose Quick, Standard or Deep per repository. Anthropic says most reviews now take about 6 to 10 minutes instead of about 20.

Source: Claude: Code Review is now generally available

A Gemma model on the phone spots scams in Singapore

On 14 October 2026 Google DeepMind described a Gemma model fine-tuned with the Singapore government to recognise scam conversations. It runs on the phone itself, so neither Google nor the government reads people's conversations: a light classifier screens messages first and passes suspicious ones to the model. GovTech Singapore has opened a beta of the Anti-Scam Pango app for Android users in Singapore.

Source: Google DeepMind: on-device AI scam detection with the Singapore Government

Lock the actions in your GitHub workflows

Since 14 October 2026 GitHub Actions can read a lockfile, .github/workflows/actions.lock, that records the exact commit of every action a workflow uses, so a moved tag or branch cannot change what runs. Install the gh actions-lock extension for GitHub CLI from the github/gh-actions-lock repository, generate the lockfile, review it and commit it. It is in public preview, also on Free plans. A lock pins versions but does not tell you whether an action is safe, so review it before you lock it.

item.title: Claude Haiku 5.5, and free AI scans for open source
item.description: Anthropic released Claude Haiku 5.5, a small model built to work as a subagent. Also: AI security scans for open-source projects, Copilot sandboxes, stacked pull requests, a full ultraviolet map of the sky and an EU initiative for a .IA domain.
item.content:encoded:
Anthropic released Claude Haiku 5.5, a small model built to work as a subagent. Also: AI security scans for open-source projects, Copilot sandboxes, stacked pull requests, a full ultraviolet map of the sky and an EU initiative for a .IA domain.

Claude Haiku 5.5, a small model for subagents

Fast, for high-volume work, with an effort setting

Anthropic released Claude Haiku 5.5 on 7 October 2026 and calls it the fastest and most capable small model it has released. It is built for quick, repeated work such as summaries, compaction, database queries and classification, and it "pairs well with Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 as a subagent on coding work". It is the first Haiku-class model with an adjustable effort setting. On OSWorld 2.1 it scores 72.4% against 15.7% for Haiku 4.5, and on Terminal-Bench 4.0 39.2% against 0.0%. Anthropic says plainly that Sonnet 5.5 and Opus 5.5 remain the better choice for complex agentic coding.

Source: Anthropic: Claude Haiku 5.5

In brief

Anthropic offers open-source projects free security scans

On 8 October 2026 Anthropic announced OSS Scanner, an opt-in service inspired by Google's OSS-Fuzz. Core maintainers of open-source projects can enrol, and their projects get periodic scans by Anthropic's most capable models free of charge. Each report contains an explanation, a proof of concept of how the bug could be exploited and, where possible, a suggested fix. The reports are written by the model and sent without human review; Anthropic expects more than 90% of them to be true positives.

Source: Anthropic: Anthropic's cyber mission

Copilot runs local commands in a sandbox

Since 7 October 2026 local sandboxing for GitHub Copilot is generally available in Copilot CLI, the GitHub Copilot app and VS Code sessions that use Agent Host, on Windows, macOS and Linux. Commands that Copilot starts get limited access to files and folders, to the internet and the local network, and to Git and GitHub CLI credentials. The sandbox can also cover local MCP servers and language servers. Organisations can require it and set rules that developers cannot weaken.

Source: GitHub Changelog: Local sandboxing for GitHub Copilot now generally available

Stacked pull requests for everyone on GitHub

On 6 October 2026 stacked pull requests became generally available on all github.com plans. A large change can be split into smaller, related pull requests that are reviewed separately and merged in order. During the preview, repositories that used stacks merged 9% more code than their peers. A whole stack goes through the merge queue as one group, and the gh stack extension of the GitHub CLI now works with Git worktrees.

Source: GitHub Changelog: Stacked pull requests are generally available

Microsoft grades agents by what they leave behind

On 3 October 2026 Microsoft presented ThinkingBox, which judges an agent by the final state of the backend and its side effects, not by what the agent says. Its benchmark has 507 business workflows that change data, each run 20 times from a clean backend. The best model, Claude Opus 5.5, solved 67.16% on a single try, and even the best models solved only 47.53% of the tasks in all 20 runs. About 79.9% of failures came from tool use. The code is under the MIT licence.

Sources: Hugging Face: ThinkingBox · GitHub: microsoft/thinkingbox

Claude helps draw the first full ultraviolet map of the sky

On 8 October 2026 Anthropic described how astrophysicist Brice Ménard, working with Claude, produced "the first complete map of the sky in UV light". NASA's GALEX telescope had imaged about two thirds of the sky; Claude's agents calibrated those data and merged them with other surveys. For the missing third, Claude learned how UV brightness relates to other wavelengths, and in hidden test regions its estimates came within about 10% of real measurements. The map is public, and every pixel is marked "measured" or "predicted".

Source: Anthropic: The missing map of the sky

EU registers a citizens' initiative for a .IA domain

On 6 October 2026 the European Commission registered the European Citizens' Initiative "Creation of a European Digital Space (.IA) for Sovereign AI Governance". It asks for an EU framework of trusted digital spaces and sandboxes for testing ethical AI, and for talks with ISO and ICANN/IANA to reserve the .IA domain for Europe. Registration only means the initiative is legally admissible. If the organisers collect one million signatures, with minimums in at least seven Member States, the Commission must respond.

Source: European Commission: European Citizens' Initiative on sovereign AI governance

Compare a question and an answer with EmbeddingGemma 2

Google released EmbeddingGemma 2 on 6 October 2026, an open embedding model under Apache 2.0 that puts text, images, audio, video and code into one shared space; for text alone it needs as little as 270 million parameters. Install sentence-transformers, load SentenceTransformer("google/embeddinggemma-2"), encode a question with prompt_name="SearchQuery" and a passage with prompt_name="Document", then print model.similarity(...) of the two, as the model card shows. Then swap in your own question and passages and see which one the model puts closest.

Sources: Google: EmbeddingGemma 2 · Hugging Face: google/embeddinggemma-2

item.title: Gemini 4 Argon goes to cyber defenders first, and new models
item.description: Google introduced Gemini 4 Argon and gave it first to a group of cyber defenders. Also: Claude Sonnet 5.5, GPT-6.1 Sol, Copilot that uses desktop apps, open agent models from H Company and an EU consultation on copyright and AI.
item.content:encoded:
Google introduced Gemini 4 Argon and gave it first to a group of cyber defenders. Also: Claude Sonnet 5.5, GPT-6.1 Sol, Copilot that uses desktop apps, open agent models from H Company and an EU consultation on copyright and AI.

Gemini 4 Argon goes to cyber defenders first

A frontier model for long work, released to defenders before everyone else

On 30 September 2026 Google introduced Gemini 4 Argon, its frontier model for real-world coding, enterprise knowledge work and cyber defence. It first went to a set of trusted cyber defenders through Google's Fairwind Program; Google plans a wider release later, without a date. The output limit grows to one million tokens, up from 64,000. Google reports 77.9% on DeepSWE v1.1, a new state of the art, and a shared first place on CWE-bench v1 with 68%. In one example Google's agents replaced 32,000 lines of SIMD code in its open-source video decoder libgav1 with safe Rust, and the result runs 2.7 times faster than the existing Rust port with identical output.

Source: Google: Gemini 4 Argon

In brief

Claude Sonnet 5.5: faster, aimed at everyday work

Anthropic released Claude Sonnet 5.5 on 28 September 2026. It writes output more than 30% faster than Sonnet 5 and is strongest at well-scoped everyday tasks, fixing bugs and polished documents, slides and spreadsheets. Anthropic says plainly that it "doesn't advance the frontier" of its models; on Terminal-Bench 4.0 it scores 70.6% against 10.3% for Sonnet 5. It is the first Sonnet launched with cyber safeguards: higher-risk security requests fall back to Sonnet 5, while routine bug fixing is not affected.

Source: Anthropic: Claude Sonnet 5.5

OpenAI adds GPT-6.1 Sol to its API

On 29 September 2026 OpenAI released GPT-6.1 Sol in its API for complex coding and professional work. The model page describes it as "near-Astra performance for complex work", with a context window of 1,050,000 tokens and up to 128,000 output tokens. It also supports Multi-agent in beta, so the model can hand parts of a task to subagents. The same day OpenAI added computer use to its Agents API: agents can finish tasks in a browser hosted by OpenAI.

Sources: OpenAI: developer changelog · OpenAI: GPT-6.1 Sol model page

Copilot learns to use desktop apps

Since 1 October 2026 GitHub Copilot can work in desktop apps for you, as a public preview in Copilot CLI and the GitHub Copilot app on macOS and Windows. It reads what an app shows, clicks, types, scrolls and moves between apps, so it can also handle software that has no API, CLI or MCP integration. Copilot asks for approval before it controls an app, and organisations can switch the feature off. In the CLI you turn it on with /computer on.

Source: GitHub Changelog: GitHub Copilot can now interact with desktop apps

H Company opens the weights of its Holo4 agent models

On 28 September 2026 H Company published Holo4, a series of agent models that work with software through graphical interfaces, code, MCP and APIs. There are two sizes, Holo4-27B and Holo4-35B-A3B, with weights on Hugging Face. On OSWorld 2.0 the 27B model scores 61.7%, against 81.8% for Claude Opus 5.5. The licences differ: the model card of Holo4-35B-A3B says Apache 2.0, that of Holo4-27B a non-commercial CC BY-NC 4.0. H Company also publishes every trajectory behind its benchmark scores.

Sources: Hugging Face: Holo4 · Hugging Face: Holo4-35B-A3B · Hugging Face: Holo4-27B

A watermark for proteins designed with AI

On 30 September 2026 Google DeepMind introduced SynthID Bio, watermarks that sit in the biological code itself. For AlphaFold 3 the team fine-tuned a small part of the model, so its predicted structures carry the watermark whoever runs it. In the lab, watermarked protein binders against three targets matched unwatermarked ones in hit rate and binding strength. DeepMind will publish a methods paper, the code, the lab data and the weights for researchers, and says resistance to deliberate tampering is still a key challenge.

Source: Google DeepMind: Introducing SynthID Bio

EU asks about copyright and AI

On 29 September 2026 the European Commission opened a targeted consultation on how technology affects copyright. The first of its four areas is "the use of copyright-protected content in artificial intelligence"; the others are online piracy of live events, the pay of music performers and producers, and the copyright of scientific research. Developers of generative AI were among those invited to answer. The deadline, first 3 November, was extended to 10 November 2026.

Source: European Commission: feedback on the effect of technology on copyright

Run an RL environment from the Hugging Face Hub

Since 28 September 2026 reinforcement learning environments live on the Hugging Face Hub as ordinary dataset repositories, with an "RL Environments" filter and no sign-up. You can try one with Harbor, an open-source framework, without an API key: install it with uv tool install --python 3.13 'harbor==0.21.0' and run one task of Terminal-Bench 2.1 with --agent oracle --env docker, as shown in the post. The oracle agent runs the reference solution and calls no model, so you need only Docker. harbor view then shows the reward, the verifier output and the logs.

Source: Hugging Face: RL environments on the Hub

item.title: Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 on the same day
item.description: Anthropic released Claude Opus 5.5 on the day OpenAI added GPT-6 Sol and Luna to its API. Also: Grok 4.7, an enzyme system found by Claude agents, a leaders' call for control of frontier AI and agents in Dev Containers.
item.content:encoded:
Anthropic released Claude Opus 5.5 on the day OpenAI added GPT-6 Sol and Luna to its API. Also: Grok 4.7, an enzyme system found by Claude agents, a leaders' call for control of frontier AI and agents in Dev Containers.

Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 on the same day

Opus 5.5 reaches the level of Fable 5.1 on most work

Anthropic released Claude Opus 5.5 on 22 September 2026, the first model of the Claude 5.5 family. Anthropic says it performs at the level of Claude Fable 5.1 on most work and writes output more than 30% faster than Opus 5. On Terminal-Bench 4.0 it scores 66.4%, against 55.8% for Fable 5.1 and 52.3% for Opus 5. In Anthropic's automated behaviour audit it is "the strongest-performing model we've tested to date", and it tried to get around its boundaries about 85% less often than Opus 5. Anthropic also notes that the model "often suspects it is being evaluated", which makes its real-world behaviour harder to predict. Anthropic expects Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 in the coming weeks.

Source: Anthropic: Claude Opus 5.5

In brief

OpenAI adds GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna to its API

On the same day, 22 September 2026, OpenAI released two reasoning models in its API that take text and images and answer in text. GPT-6 Sol is "built to power complex coding and agentic workflows", and GPT-6 Luna is OpenAI's "most efficient model for focused, high-volume tasks". Both have a context window of 1,050,000 tokens and up to 128,000 output tokens. In the Responses API Sol can use tools such as web search, a hosted shell, computer use and MCP.

Sources: OpenAI: API changelog · OpenAI: GPT-6 Sol · OpenAI: GPT-6 Luna

Grok 4.7 for coding and knowledge work

xAI published Grok 4.7 on 21 September 2026; the announcement calls it the company's most powerful model for coding and knowledge work. It is built on a new, larger base model than Grok 4.6 and trained with a longer reinforcement learning run on harder tasks, many of which take hours. On Terminal-Bench 4.0 it scores 37.6%, up from 20.3% for Grok 4.6. It is available in Cursor, Grok Build and the Grok API.

Source: xAI: Grok 4.7

Claude agents find an unknown enzyme system

On 23 September 2026 Anthropic reported that Claude found a family it calls "array-associated reverse transcriptases" (ART): a reverse transcriptase, a partner gene of unknown purpose and a long array of evenly spaced DNA repeats. About 950 agents worked for 21 hours, gathered over 200,000 reverse transcriptases, found 3,500 candidates and wrote up the 20 most promising. In the first lab tests by human scientists the array is expressed as a set of distinct short RNAs. What the system does is still unknown.

Source: Anthropic: Claude discovers a novel enzyme system

Leaders call for control of frontier AI

On 22 September 2026 a statement signed by 22 leaders, among them the President of the European Commission, called for frontier AI to stay "under human direction, oversight and control". It asks companies for transparent safety protocols with mandatory testing before release and independent evaluation, and governments for common standards and shared reports of serious safety incidents. It also asks UN member states to explore an international institution that could set standards and enable verification. The statement remains open to other leaders.

Source: Government of the Netherlands: A call for control of frontier AI models

VS Code 1.139 runs agents in Dev Containers on remote hosts

VS Code 1.139, released on 23 September 2026, lets agents run inside a project's Dev Container on SSH, Tunnel and WSL hosts, not only in local folders. The feature is rolling out gradually behind the setting chat.agentHost.devContainer.enabled and needs Docker on the remote host. A new agent host runs agents in a separate process, so several windows can join the same session, and the session list opens about 12 times faster.

Source: Visual Studio Code: September 2026 (version 1.139)

Google adds encrypted memory to Private AI Compute

On 23 September 2026 Google DeepMind added persistent memory to Private AI Compute, which until then forgot everything at the end of a task. The memory sits in dedicated, encrypted storage, and the keys are held only on the user's own devices. Data is decrypted briefly inside a hardware-isolated secure enclave and encrypted again. Google publishes a tamper-proof public record of its server software, an updated technical brief and the results of an independent audit.

Source: Google DeepMind: Advancing Private AI Compute with secure server-side memory
